items.title: Nepal Police — DNA profiling for unidentified remains
items.summary: Nepal Police asks relatives of people missing after the Rasuwa / Bhote Koshi floods to help identify recovered bodies through DNA. In Nepal: first-degree relatives (father, mother, son or daughter) can give a fresh blood sample plus two passport-size photos at Nepal Police Hospital Pathology Lab, Maharajgunj, or the nearest District Police Office. items.source: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA)
items.title: NDRRMA — Bhotekoshi water level rising again (31 Aug)
items.summary: On Sunday 31 August, NDRRMA warned that water levels in the flooded Bhotekoshi River had risen again and urged residents and rescue personnel in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and nearby areas to take precaution. Agency said it would issue further updates after receiving additional information. Death toll and missing figures were also being updated on ndrrma.gov.np — always confirm on the original notice board.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — public warning via official channels

items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: GYIRONG, Xizang, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- Rescue operations intensified Thursday at the mudslide-stricken border port of Gyirong in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, as rescue teams and helicopters were dispatched to the disaster area. The first team of 141 rescuers arrived at the port on Thursday morning after the disaster caused significant casualties along the China-Nepal border, according to China's Ministry of Emergency Management.
items.citation: Xinhua (Gyirong / Tibet side) — FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang

items.title: Nepal Police official found and missing lists
items.summary: Nepal Police maintains the official Unified Database for missing persons, found persons, and unidentified remains related to the flood-affected areas. Search at udb.nepalpolice.gov.np/missing and udb.nepalpolice.gov.np/found. Official confirmation of status comes only from Nepal Police — not from volunteer sites or social media.
